reasoning: Roofline reports compute bottleneck with Compute SOL 88.1% vs Memory SOL 42.4%. Kernel metrics match this: sm__throughput is 88.14% of peak while dram throughput is only 42.45%, and tensor pipe usage is 0%, so FP32/VALU math is the limiter rather than DRAM.

root_causes.cause: Heavy FP32 VALU workload from fused FC1/SiLU/FC2 and reduction structure saturates vector ALU pipelines.

evidence.interpretation: Most executed instructions are VALU, indicating arithmetic pressure dominates execution.

fixes.fix: Reduce FP32 instruction count by restructuring dot-product accumulation (larger vectorized K tiles / unrolling with fewer reduction ops) and fusing scale application more efficiently.
fixes.rationale: Lowering per-output arithmetic and reduction overhead reduces VALU pressure, increasing headroom in a compute-bound kernel.

root_causes.cause: No matrix/tensor-core style acceleration path is used; all math runs on standard compute pipelines.

evidence.interpretation: Tensor/matrix pipelines are completely unused, so throughput is limited to non-tensor ALU performance.

fixes.fix: Retarget matmul portions (FC1/FC2) to MFMA/tensor-instruction-friendly kernels (e.g., Triton block GEMM or rocWMMA-compatible path) with supported datatypes/accumulation strategy.
fixes.rationale: Moving dense matrix work to matrix engines increases effective compute throughput and relieves standard VALU bottlenecks.
